_note: NFL values; each number was parsed from the quoted sentence (see _quotes).

_quotes.length_ft: Other variants of American football such as [[nine-man football|nine-man]] or [[arena football]] typically use smaller fields with smaller end zones. ==Field description== [[File:Estadio emilio royo.jpg|thumb|Emilio Royo stadium in Panama City]] The entire field is a rectangle {{convert|360|ft|m}} long by {{convert|160|ft|m}} wide, covering a total of 1.32 acres.<ref name="foo">{{Cite web|url=https://www.networldsports.com/buyers-guides/football-field-dimensions-guide|title = Football Field Dimensions}}</ref> The two longer lines of the field perimeter are known as sidelines and the two shorter ones are called end lines.
_quotes.width_ft: Other variants of American football such as [[nine-man football|nine-man]] or [[arena football]] typically use smaller fields with smaller end zones. ==Field description== [[File:Estadio emilio royo.jpg|thumb|Emilio Royo stadium in Panama City]] The entire field is a rectangle {{convert|360|ft|m}} long by {{convert|160|ft|m}} wide, covering a total of 1.32 acres.<ref name="foo">{{Cite web|url=https://www.networldsports.com/buyers-guides/football-field-dimensions-guide|title = Football Field Dimensions}}</ref> The two longer lines of the field perimeter are known as sidelines and the two shorter ones are called end lines.
_quotes.end_zone_yd: Most distances on a football field are expressed in terms of [[yard]]s. The goal lines span the width of the field and run {{convert|10|yd|m}} parallel to each end line.
_quotes.yard_line_interval_yd: Additional lines span the width of the field at 5-yard intervals from each goal line. ===End zones=== {{Main|End zone}} The areas at each end of the field between the goal lines and end lines – including the goal lines themselves – are called the [[end zone]]s.
_quotes.hash_from_sideline_ft: In the NFL since 1972, the hash marks are {{convert|70|ft|9|in|m}} from each sideline; in college football they are {{convert|60|ft|m}} from each sideline.
_quotes.hash_tick_ft: Between the 5-yard lines they are marked with 2-foot lines painted perpendicular to the sidelines at 1-yard intervals.
_quotes.goalpost_width_ft: Team or league logos or other patterns may be painted inside the end zone as long as they do not interfere with the mandatory field markings. ===Goals=== {{See also|Goal (sports)}} A [[goal (sports)|goal]] is centered on each end line, consisting of a horizontal crossbar {{convert|10|ft|m}} above the ground and aligned with the inside edge of the end line, with vertical goal posts (colloquially "uprights") at each end of the crossbar {{convert|18|ft|6|in|m}} apart and extending at least {{convert|35|ft|m}} above the crossbar in the NFL.
_quotes.crossbar_height_ft: There is a [[goal (sports)|goal]] centered on each end line, with a crossbar {{convert|10|ft|m}} above the ground and goalposts {{convert|18|ft|6|in|m}} apart (in college and the [[NFL]]) extending at least {{convert|35|ft|m}} above the crossbar.
_quotes.boundary_line_ft: NFL rules call for the sidelines and end lines to be {{convert|6|ft|m}} wide, though the lines may be narrower on fields used for multiple sports or by college or amateur teams.
_quotes.number_bottom_from_sideline_yd: NFL rules call for the bottom edge of each number to be 12 yards from the sideline.
_quotes.try_line_ft: The college football standard, which was the previous standard in the NFL (from {{nfly|1945}} to {{nfly|1971}}), is 40 feet apart (20 yards from the sidelines),<ref>{{cite magazine|title=High On The Hash |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1086452/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100729002927/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1086452/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 29, 2010 | magazine=Sports Illustrated |via=(CNN)| date=August 28, 1972}}</ref> instituted in [[1993 NCAA Division I-A football season|1993]].<ref name=mhmsooff>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=a6IaAAAAIBAJ&sjid=niwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4236%2C2591064 |newspaper=Milwaukee Journal |last=Chaptman |first=Dennis |title=Moving hash marks should open offenses |date=March 26, 1993 |page=C2}}</ref><ref name=nrtkcot>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=WEZWAAAAIBAJ&sjid=duoDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5387%2C406590 |newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |last=Clark |first=Bob |title=New rules to keep coaches on toes |date=September 2, 1993 |page=9F }}</ref> Previously, the college width was the same as the high school standard, at one-third of the width of the field (53{{frac|1|3}} feet). ===Other markings=== In the NFL, a {{convert|3|ft|m|adj=on}} line is painted parallel to the goal line at the center of the 2-yard line; this denotes the line of scrimmage for a [[two-point conversion]] attempt (this was also the line of scrimmage for an [[conversion (gridiron football)|extra point]] attempt prior to 2015); at the college level, this special hashmark is on the 3-yard line for an [[conversion (gridiron football)|extra point]] attempt. A small X may be painted at the center of each 35-yard line on NFL or college fields to indicate the spot where [[kickoff (gridiron football)|kickoffs]] take place. Most professional and collegiate fields have a team or league logo painted at the 50-yard line.
